messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT OPENED — INC-20260315-1
incident-bot: Pager: SRE oncall @maria. Alert: KV cache tail latency spike on inference-runtime-prod — sustained for 5m, 500+ distinct hosts. Severity: P0.

maria: Ack — I'm on it. Thanks bot. Jumping into dashboards now (https://grafana.internal/redwood/runtime).

aj: I can help with logs. I'm seeing a flood of `kv_cache_read_timeout` entries across pods 12-18 in eu-west. Attaching quick query I ran in our ES cluster:

```
// Elasticsearch pseudo-query
GET /logs/_search
{ "query": { "bool": { "must": [ { "match": { "service": "inference-runtime" }}, { "match": { "message": "kv_cache_read_timeout" }}, { "range": { "@timestamp": { "gte": "now-10m" }}} ] } } }
```

aj: Rough counts: ~2.1k events / 10m window, spike correlates with 5xx rate on route /v1/generate.

maria: Good find. Any customer-facing errors? sre-ops, do we have elevated 5xxs per-customer?

sre-ops: Yes — we see a cluster-level increase in 5xxs. Top affected tenants: onboarding-corp (20% of spike) and finapp-prod (15%). Error pattern: upstream KV read timeouts cascading into request timeouts.

sarah: Noted — I already opened a support ticket for finapp-prod and flagged for high priority. They're seeing timeouts in their user sessions.

maria: Live mitigation plan: 1) Add a temporary alert suppressor for kv_cache_read_timeout noise so we don't page repeatedly. 2) Increase route-level request timeout to allow graceful fallback for affected pods. 3) Deploy a kernel-level quick patch (if safe) to backoff KV clients. 4) Update log alert rule to reduce noise by filtering known benign shard-opening messages.

aj: For (1) I can add a suppression in the alert manager: mute alerts with label `error:kv_cache_read_timeout` for 15m with an expiry. Will do now.

aj: Done — suppression applied: `mute: {matchers: [{name: "error", value: "kv_cache_read_timeout"}], endsAt: now+15m }` :white_check_mark:

eng-infra-bot: Deploy check: rolling config update to route timeouts queued (change id cfg-20260315-3). CI checks passed.

maria: Pushing timeout change to canary (2 pods) first. If canary looks good for 3m we'll roll.

aj: While rolling, I'm going to refine the log-based alert rule. Current rule fires on any `kv_cache_read_timeout` occurrence — too noisy. Proposed new query (Datadog-style) to only alert when the noise correlates with request 5xxs at host-level:

```
logs("service:inference-runtime AND status:5xx AND message:kv_cache_read_timeout").rollup("count", 300) >= 50
```

aj: Additionally propose a regex to exclude benign messages emitted during shard_open operations that are non-impactful:

```
# regex to filter shard-opening benign noise
message !~ /kv_cache_read_timeout: shard_opening/  
```

maria: That seems reasonable. Two things: add a signature that checks for repeated timeouts from same host within 1m window (to catch true failures), and keep a lower-severity metric alert for aggregate error rate.

aj: Implemented both: 1) Updated log alert rule to require >=50 matching events across <=5 hosts in 5m to trigger P1. 2) Added host-repeat rule: host_count(kv_cache_read_timeout, 60s) >= 5 -> P0.

sre-ops: Verified new rule saved as `log-alerts/runtime-kv-timeout-v2`. Linking: https://monitoring.internal/alerts/runtime-kv-timeout-v2

maria: Canary timeout change looks stable after 4m, rolling to remaining nodes now. No increase in tail latencies.

aj: Data after suppression + timeout roll: 5xxs dropped 70% compared to peak, request success rate recovering. KV timeout logs still present but mostly tagged `shard_opening` which we filtered out.

sarah: Customer updates: finapp-prod acknowledged workaround and will monitor. Onboarding-corp interested in SLA credit — flagged for CS.

maria: Great. Now for post-incident follow-ups (action items):
- aj -> add a deterministic signature in the ingestion pipeline to label `kv_cache_shard_open` vs `kv_cache_timeout` so alerts only fire on true timeouts.
- eng-infra -> investigate recent cluster topology change that coincided with spike (assigned to eng-infra team).
- sre-ops -> add a dashboard panel showing host-level repeat-timeout counts to simplify future triage.
- maria -> write a short blameless incident note with timeline and mitigation steps.

aj: I'll own the ingestion signature change, ETA EOD. Regex and rule changes are already in staging and will be promoted to prod after a quick review.

eng-infra-bot: Noted. I'll look at the recent autoscaler and shard rebalancer jobs run at ~18:12 UTC that overlap with incident start.

tariq: I'm on next shift — handover: gave readout, suppression window expires at +15m from now (watch window). If anything flares, escalate to me.

maria: Thanks @tariq — handing off. Final checks: confirm suppression expiry, ensure host-repeat P0 rule is active, release suppressed alerts once we're comfortable.

aj: All set from my side. Suppression expiry: 1801113310 (15m). Host-repeat P0 rule active and verified.

maria: Closing incident channel now, moving to postmortem doc draft: https://wiki.internal/incidents/INC-20260315-1. If you have logs or graphs to attach, drop them in that doc. :memo:

incident-bot: INCIDENT CLOSED — condition resolved and mitigations applied.

sre-ops: Postmortem scheduled for tomorrow 10:00 UTC in #incidents.

maria: Thanks all for quick response. Main takeaway: tighten log signatures + add host-repeat detection to prevent noisy pages.

tariq: :thumbsup:
